title: Classical cohomology is closed under ambient sums, triangles and pullback
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite commutative ring $A$ with $\ell^n1_A=0$ for some $n\geq1$, and a scheme $T$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and unbounded derived categories on the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $\mathcal C_T$ consist of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are classical, meaning they lie in the essential image of $\nu_T^*$ on étale module sheaves [sk-def-pe-classical-definition] [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Then $\mathcal C_T$ is full replete, triangulated, closed under all small ambient coproducts and under canonical truncations. Cohomology and canonical truncations commute with these coproducts. For every scheme map $r:W\to T$, constant-coefficient inverse image $r^*$ takes $\mathcal C_T$ into $\mathcal C_W$ and commutes with truncations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. If $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))\subseteq\mathcal C_T$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible] [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B_T$ be the full replete subcategory of classical constant-$A$ module sheaves. By [det-pe-classical-derived-weak-serre] it contains zero and is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions. Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to the abelian category of pro-étale constant-$A$ modules and $\mathcal B_T$. Its $D_{\mathcal B_T}$ is exactly $\mathcal C_T$, so $\mathcal C_T$ is full replete and triangulated. The formulas in [def-kun-truncations] show that canonical truncation retains a cohomology sheaf or replaces it by zero in every degree; thus both canonical truncations preserve $\mathcal C_T$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory; canonical truncation formulas of def-kun-truncations

proof.text:
Classical sheaves are closed under arbitrary small sums in the ambient heart. Indeed write $F_i\simeq
u_T^*E_i$ by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. The two module categories have small coproducts by their existing small-colimit instances. For any pro-étale module sheaf $G$, the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] gives naturally
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_T^*( igoplus_iE_i),G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}( igoplus_iE_i,
u_{T,*}G)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(
u_T^*E_i,G).$$
Consequently $
u_T^*( igoplus_iE_i)$, with its canonical coprojections, is the ambient coproduct of the $F_i$ and is classical. The same calculation includes the empty family. In Lean use the constant-module encoding equivalence and closure of the essential image of the fully faithful comparison left adjoint under colimits.

source.place: Module comparison adjunction and its elementary coproduct universal-property calculation

proof.text: Use the proved source-library homology-coproduct instance [src-weil-derived-homology-preserves-coproducts], which derives exact termwise coproducts from K-injective resolutions and AB4. Grothendieck module sheaves have AB5 and hence AB4. Apply the heart coproduct result degreewise. For either truncation, compose with every homology functor: in the retained range the canonical inclusion or projection is an isomorphism, and outside it every object is zero. Thus these composites preserve coproducts. Homology functors jointly reflect isomorphisms and hence jointly detect colimit cocones, proving preservation by truncation itself. All helper results are proved privately in the item module; no new statement is left unfinished.

proof.text:
For any scheme morphism $r:W	o T$, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives exact constant-coefficient inverse image, induced termwise on complexes. Thus the kernel/image/quotient formula for cohomology gives $\mathcal H^q(r^*K)\simeq r^*\mathcal H^q(K)$. If $\mathcal H^q(K)\simeq
u_T^*E_q$, the fixed-module comparison square together with [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-pullback-encoding] gives $r^*
u_T^*E_q\simeq
u_W^*r_{\mathrm{ét}}^*E_q$, a classical sheaf. Hence $r^*K\in\mathcal C_W$. Exactness also preserves the kernel and cokernel in the good truncation formulas [def-kun-truncations], so the termwise identifications give $r^*	au_{\le a}K\simeq	au_{\le a}r^*K$ and $r^*	au_{\ge a}K\simeq	au_{\ge a}r^*K$. Only the unrestricted inverse-image clause of the comparison is used; no qcqs condition on $r$ is needed. The actual coefficient-pullback square is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-pullback-encoding], combined with the fixed-module comparison square. The exact-functor derived truncation isomorphisms satisfy the canonical equations by the truncation lift and descent identities.

source.place: Commutative comparison square and exact inverse images; elementary truncation calculation

proof.text: The canonical integralModelIntrinsicRealization factors through the section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding], restriction to constant scalars, and intrinsic sheafification. Its underlying additive sheaf is naturally isomorphic to the original internal-module sheaf, using the sheafification unit. The forgetful functors preserve finite limits and coproducts and reflect isomorphisms; consequently constant-scalar restriction and the realization are exact and preserve coproducts. On qcqs T, a generator has cohomology with finite constant models. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], these are locally finitely presented; transport through the canonical coefficient pullback yields internal constructibility on the same strata. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-constructible-encoding] using [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding], the finite discrete point-ring identification, and [lem-weil-pbc-internal-module-ab-equivalence]. The resulting fixed-module sheaf is constructible, so [lem-weil-pbc-fixed-module-constructible-origin] places it in the essential image of etale comparison. Its underlying sheaf is therefore classical. The forgetful comparison of the encoding and the underlying-sheaf isomorphism of the canonical realization transfer classicality to the required cohomology sheaf. No Tor bound is used.

source.place: Constructible classicality for qcqs schemes and discrete Noetherian rings; finite-coefficient identifications

proof.text: By steps 1 and 3, $\mathcal C_T$ is a full replete triangulated subcategory closed under all small ambient coproducts. By step 5 it contains $\Dctf(T,A)$. The definition [sk-def-localizing-closure] is the intersection of all full replete triangulated subcategories with exactly these containment and coproduct properties. In particular that intersection is contained in $\mathcal C_T$, giving $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))\subseteq\mathcal C_T$. Formally pull back the already proved ordinary classical localizing class along the derived realization. Exactness makes this inverse image triangulated; coproduct preservation makes it localizing. Step 5 gives its containment of the generators. Apply the intersection definition and then the homology comparison isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Six steps prove all closure, commutation, pullback and localizing-containment clauses using existing nodes only. The argument distinguishes weak Serre closure from full faithfulness, computes exact ambient sums termwise, and uses the heart constructible comparison only under qcqs and Noetherian hypotheses. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Transfer paragraph of det-ctf-finite-proper-localizing, specifically the classical-cohomology closure argument isolated as old split step 4. It does not assume that all unbounded étale objects are generated by Dctf or that unbounded derived comparison is an equivalence.

tool_uses.why: Heart-level weak Serre closure of classical modules is the generic comparison tool needed for the classical-cohomology subcategory; it does not replace the unit proper-pushforward argument.
Generic derived-category criterion converts heart weak Serre closure to triangulated closure; no result of this proper-image unit supplies that criterion.
Generic existence of small coproducts in the two module-sheaf categories is needed for the explicit adjunction calculation.
Generic termwise computation of unbounded derived coproducts is needed; it does not use any geometric proper-image theorem.
Only the unrestricted exact inverse-image square is used to pull back a classical heart sheaf; no direct-image assertion is used.
Its heart clause supplies classicality of finite-coefficient constructible sheaves in the Transfer paragraph.
